claims.text: MoNbTaTiW is a refractory high-entropy alloy suitable for the proposed treatment.
The untreated MoNbTaTiW surface exhibits normal high-temperature oxidation behavior.
Pack-cementation at approximately 950°C for 6 hours in an inert atmosphere will deposit an aluminide coating on MoNbTaTiW.
During high-temperature exposure, the aluminide coating will produce a continuous, dense, and adherent alpha-Al2O3 scale.
The aluminide coating acts as a surface aluminum reservoir.
Aluminum from the coating diffuses to the surface and reacts with oxygen.
The reaction of aluminum with oxygen under the stated conditions forms stable, slow-growing alpha-Al2O3.
The alumina scale acts as a barrier to further oxygen ingress.
The alumina scale minimizes oxide-scale spallation.
Aluminizing will substantially improve the oxygen resistance of MoNbTaTiW relative to the untreated alloy.
The aluminized alloy will exhibit significantly lower oxidation weight gain than the untreated alloy.
The aluminized alloy will develop a thinner oxide scale than the untreated alloy.
The oxide on the aluminized alloy will have fewer defects and better adherence than that on the untreated alloy.
Untreated refractory high-entropy alloys typically oxidize rapidly and form thicker, less protective scales that may spall.
The intervention should be effective during exposure to air at 1200°C for approximately 100 hours.
Effectiveness at longer exposure times, higher temperatures, or in other atmospheres is unverified.
The magnitude of the oxidation improvement and coating uniformity may vary with aluminizing process parameters.
Variability in scale adhesion and pack-cementation residues may affect experimental results.
